column1: What share of US occupational tasks are plausibly automatable with current AI, per McKinsey/MIT-style analyses?
What is the range for customer-support ticket resolution without human escalation at large deployments in 2026?
column2: 10–40%, varying widely by domain; climbs past 50% on narrow product-support corpora.

column1: Which two data sources does the chapter cite for the slowdown in entry-level software-developer postings?
column2: BLS (Bureau of Labor Statistics) and Indeed Hiring Lab.

column1: What does the chapter call the category of work most directly affected by AI?
column2: Routine cognitive labour — tasks that follow patterns, can be specified in writing, and produce text or structured data.

column1: Name the five historical 'wires' the chapter references when framing AI as a general-purpose-technology transition.
column2: The telegraph, the telephone, the internet, the smartphone, and now AI (the fifth wire).

column1: What is happening to mid-tier SaaS margins, per the chapter?
column2: They are being compressed — products sold for $50/seat/month face undercutting at $5/seat/month or in-house AI builds, reducing pricing power.

column1: What distinguishes high-margin new software from squeezed software in the chapter's framing?
column2: High-margin software integrates AI as its core capability (coding assistants, design tools, research platforms); squeezed software is boring SaaS whose functionality AI commoditizes.

column1: What does the chapter say about long-tail publishers relying on search referral?
column2: Many are in serious distress; some are pivoting to direct content-licensing deals with model providers as the new revenue path.

column1: What is the chapter's honest caveat on forecasts beyond three years?
column2: Forecasts more than three years out are not honest — stated explicitly in the 'who keeps what' section.

column1: What does the chapter identify as the actual policy challenge of this decade?
column2: The gap between the speed of technology change and the pace of the institutions designed to respond — labour markets, education, social safety nets, antitrust — which are several years to a decade slower.
